newsitem.title: USA: Oscar-winning figures returned to creator.
newsitem.headline: Oscar-winning figures returned to creator.

text.p: Wallace and Gromit, two plasticine figures that starred in last year's Oscar-winning short "A Close Shave", were returned to their creator on Monday after being left in the trunk of a taxi over the weekend.

British creator Nick Park said Wallace and his dog Gromit were returned on Monday morning by the taxi driver who drove Park to his Manhattan hotel on Saturday when he arrived in New York for a publicity tour.
"I couldn't believe it," Park told Reuters television. "He didn't seem to want to stick around. I shook his hand, offered him an award, but he wouldn't hear of it."

Park, who described the unidentified cab driver as "extremely decent", said he thought he would never again see the original Wallace and Gromit figures on their red motorcycle and sidecar after leaving them in a case in the trunk of the taxi. A porter at the hotel failed to notice the case in the cab's trunk and the driver drove away with them.

Park said he spent the rest of the weekend calling police precincts and taxi companies, faxing them drawings of the nine-inch (23 cm) figures, among the best-loved animated screen stars in Britain and the United States.
The puppets have starred in such hit short films as "The Wrong Trousers," "A Grand Day Out," and "A Close Shave," which won an Oscar in 1996 for Best Animated Short Film.
